title: Testing and Quality Assurance
concept: **Quality** means how well a product, system, or process meets the requirements and satisfies the customer. **Quality Assurance (QA)** focuses on the **process**. Its goal is to make sure we follow the right process to prevent problems and produce a quality product. **Quality Control (QC)** focuses on the **product**. It checks whether the finished product meets the required quality standards. **Testing** is a part of QC. Testing checks the actual product to find bugs and make sure it works as expected. The relationship is: **QA → QC → Testing** QA focuses on **preventing defects by improving the process**. QC focuses on **checking the product for defects**. Testing is one of the main activities used in QC to find those defects. A mature organisation uses all three: **QA to prevent problems, QC to check the product, and testing to find bugs.**
keyPoints: QA is process-oriented and aims to provide confidence quality requirements will be met; QC is product-oriented and verifies they were met.
Testing is a form of quality control — a product-focused activity that examines the test object dynamically or statically.
Effective quality management uses both QA (process discipline) and QC (testing and other product checks).

quiz.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between Quality Assurance (QA), Quality Control (QC), and testing?
options: QA, QC, and testing are three synonyms for the same activity.
Testing is a form of QC, which is product-focused; QA is process-focused and aims to provide confidence that quality requirements will be met.
QA performs all dynamic testing; QC performs only static reviews.
Testing replaces the need for QA in agile teams.
quiz.explanation: QA is process-focused (improving how software is built), QC is product-focused (checking the product against requirements), and testing is one kind of QC activity. None of these activities replaces the others.
